title: Choose the visual world
question: Which world best turns Daniel's problem-solving approach into an experience a prospective client will remember?

options.label: Signal Path
options.lineage: metropolitan control maps and live service diagrams
options.thesis: Every engagement becomes a route from ambiguity to a dependable outcome.
options.viewport: A full-screen route map crosses Daniel's oversized name, moving through Clarify, Model, Build, Stress, and Ship before terminating at Start a project.
options.risk: The map must remain an explanation of real work, never decorative transit cosplay.

raised.raise: The route field now owns the full viewport and uses depth to establish a memorable sense of scale.
Every status, number, and active state must be tied to evidence already present in the portfolio.
Type responds to the route's current problem stage so the interaction changes hierarchy, not just decoration.
One decisive state system distinguishes live focus, completed work, and supporting detail.

options.label: Incident Ledger
options.lineage: incident command boards, annotated runbooks, and shift logs
options.thesis: The portfolio reads as a calm record of complex situations brought back under control.
options.viewport: A large active incident sheet pairs Daniel's portrait with a precise problem, intervention, and stabilized-state sequence.
options.risk: This is highly legible but closer to the familiar B2B operations aesthetic many technical portfolios already use.

options.label: Variable Engineer
options.thesis: Daniel's engineering range is demonstrated by a typographic system that adapts as the problem changes.
options.viewport: One enormous responsive phrase changes weight and width while the visitor moves between frontend, backend, QA, and reliability work.
options.case: It identifies strongly with frontend craft and creates an excellent interaction, but explains systems problem-solving less directly than Signal Path.
options.risk: The typographic idea could imply a design-specialist portfolio before the engineering breadth becomes clear.

options.label: Night Shift Network
options.lineage: a rain-dark city moving from blue hour to dawn
options.thesis: Projects become illuminated systems kept alive through the night.
options.viewport: A nocturnal systems landscape reveals work as lights and routes across a city.
options.case: The atmosphere is memorable, but the metaphor delays Daniel's offer and makes the work harder to scan.
options.risk: A beautiful city can become the subject instead of Daniel's work.

options.label: Proof Counter
options.thesis: Evidence arrives as physical counts inside a precise instrument panel.
options.viewport: Six projects and five-plus years glow as layered numerical evidence beside a concise offer.
options.case: The engineering association is immediate, but the portfolio does not yet contain enough quantified outcomes to sustain the system honestly.
options.risk: Retro instrumentation would overpower the limited set of factual metrics.

options.label: Raku Process
options.thesis: Each system is shaped through heat, uncertainty, and controlled intervention.
options.viewport: A vessel-like project object moves through exposed process stages.
options.case: The process metaphor is rich, but prospective software clients would need to decode too much before understanding the offer.
options.risk: Material beauty would outrun product clarity.

options.label: Emergency Broadcast
options.thesis: Complex delivery becomes a sequence of calm, unmistakable instructions.
options.viewport: A hard-cut briefing names the problem, maps the response, and points directly to the next action.
options.case: The hierarchy is powerful, but emergency language misrepresents collaborative freelance work as perpetual crisis response.
options.kept: Decisive hierarchy across active and supporting states.
options.risk: The alarm grammar could feel aggressive and theatrical.

options.label: Systems Expedition
options.thesis: Every project is an expedition through layered technical terrain.
options.viewport: Layered system planes rise above one direct invitation to explore Daniel's work.
options.case: The composition is memorable, but the travel metaphor adds distance instead of clarifying Daniel's problem-solving process.
options.kept: One dominant focal move with disciplined cropping.
options.risk: The illustration style could read as a campaign poster rather than an engineering portfolio.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished developer portfolio with a concise hero, selected-work grid, skills, experience, and contact CTA.
canonCard.viewport: Daniel's name, role, short introduction, portrait, and a clear View work button in a familiar split hero.
canonCard.risk: Clear and usable, but structurally indistinguishable from thousands of other software portfolios.
